messages.subject: Re: Milkweed for my area
messages.text:
Hi Michelle,

Sorry for the long wait before getting back to you, things have been very busy on our end and I should have replied sooner.

For Berkeley County, West Virginia, you're in a zone that supports all of our common species well. Here are my recommendations depending on your situation:

- Asclepias syriaca (Common milkweed): the most vigorous, spreads readily, great for larger spaces or naturalized areas. Excellent for monarchs.
- Asclepias incarnata (Swamp milkweed): more compact, tolerates both wet and drier soils, easier to manage in a garden bed, and also very attractive to monarchs and other pollinators.
- Asclepias tuberosa (Butterfly weed): beautiful orange flowers, very drought-tolerant, stays put (doesn't spread), ideal for sunny dry spots.

If you want something easy and versatile, incarnata is usually the one I suggest first: it germinates well, doesn't take over, and thrives in a wide range of conditions.

You can find our seed packets here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/milkweed-seeds

If you'd like, tell me a bit about your spot (sunny and dry, or damp?) and I can narrow it down further.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
